recipe.notes:
Score = sigmoid(yes_logit / 5) at the last prompt position ("Yes" is single token 9454; the repo's own pad token is the id-151643 end-of-text special; padding/truncation right). The prompt is ChatML: system=query, user=document, ending with the assistant header whose trailing newline is the token the score is pooled from.
template.jinja is REQUIRED and load bearing (R10): the tokenizer's own chat template is refused on the score path (io_processor.py:701-710), and without a template file vLLM silently tokenizes query and document as a pair - no warning fires for this converted architecture (the warning needs is_original_qwen3_reranker, io_processor.py:460-476). Serve-time smoke check for the GPU wave: boot with serve_argv, then POST /rerank for one short pair and require the reply's relevance_score in (0, 1); a dropped template file scores a raw logit-shaped number outside (0, 1) or errors. The template's declared normalisation (client.template normalize: [strip] = the paper's query.strip()/doc.strip()): fit strips the content spans before measuring, the wire ships the stripped spans, the reference's spans (the paper's own strip) agree on every under-cap row, and the template file carries no jinja trim filter anywhere (measured token-id equal on the whitespace-padded case too, r-zerank1 check_cpu.py 21/21). The template check compares raw against raw and passes on any pairs file. The vendor zerank-2 chat_template.jinja is NOT reusable: it emits the assistant header only under add_generation_prompt, which vLLM's rerank path never passes, so the header (the anchor) is lost - 4/7 measured rows fail; hence the shipped file.
Over-cap behaviour is the one declared reference deviation: the paper right-cuts the whole rendered prompt at 8192 tokens and drops the assistant header (the anchor); the served path reserves the frame, cuts the content spans only, and re-attaches the header - declared as reference.known_deviations: [anchor_drop_over_cap]: stage 1 and stage 2 report the over-cap rows in a non-gating table and gate the under-cap rows exactly. reference.py's --mode render writes the paper's own cut as the content spans (raw character offsets of the whole-prompt right cut); it never ports the client's cut. Settle rule (read from the merged rerank client, one rule for the family): the pair fit binds on overflow; the client settles the shared query once per request, at its declared query_max_tokens share whenever the query exceeds it. A query over the 4096-token share therefore ships cut at the share while the in-process reference keeps it whole: over-share queries are declared divergence rows - an over-share query in an UNDER-budget pair is an under-cap row and gates red by design (the reference never ports the client's settle rule), so the wave's pairs files keep queries well within the share and drop any row stage 1 goes red on. The score head runs fp32 (the pooling runner's default) against the paper's bf16 lm_head logits: served scores are more precise, not bit-equal; the probability gates (|delta| <= 0.02 for 99%, <= 0.05 max) bound it (research risk R4). Datasets with run-level instructions: the paper scored the bare query; this recipe pins instruction: none so the served path does the same - nothing folds Task:/Query: (research R3). trust_remote_code stays false: with auto_map present and modeling_zeranker.py staged, AutoConfig resolves native Qwen3Config (measured), so the remote code is never executed. Post-serve, wave T0 must GET /v1/models and fire one /rerank; the recorder's exchanges cover the route.
